chapter: Lecture 5: Weathering of Rocks and Minerals — Types, Physical & Biological Agents
subject: agricultural_chemistry_and_soil_science

questions.stem: What geological term describes the unconsolidated mantle of weathered rock debris resting above unaltered parent bedrock?
questions.rationale: Regolith is the unconsolidated residue of weathered rock resting on the Earth's surface above solid bedrock. (Key Takeaway: Regolith is the unconsolidated mantle of weathered rock material.)

questions.stem: Which fundamental process of weathering brings about mechanical breakdown into smaller particles without changing chemical composition?
questions.rationale: Physical weathering causes mechanical disintegration such as cracking and crushing with zero chemical composition change. (Key Takeaway: Physical weathering alters physical geometry only without changing mineral chemistry.)

questions.stem: Among all physical weathering agents, which agent exerts the most pronounced and widespread disintegrating effect on Earth?
questions.rationale: Water is the pre-eminent physical weathering agent, acting continuously as a disintegrating, transporting, and abrasive medium. (Key Takeaway: Water is the most active and widespread physical weathering agent.)

questions.stem: By what percentage does liquid water expand in volume upon freezing into crystalline ice?
questions.rationale: Water expands by precisely 9 percent in volume when freezing into crystalline ice. (Key Takeaway: Phase transition to ice increases water volume by 9 percent.)

questions.stem: What geomorphic term describes the concentric peeling away of outer curved rock shells from parent bedrock due to thermal stresses?
questions.rationale: Exfoliation (onion-skin weathering) is the peeling of outer curved rock sheets caused by differential expansion between heated surfaces and cool inner rock layers. (Key Takeaway: Exfoliation peels concentric outer shells from parent rock.)

questions.stem: In which Indian geographic regions are classic wind-sculpted Mushroom Rocks prominently observed?

options.B: Aravalis and Thar Desert of Rajasthan

questions.correct_answer: B) Aravalis and Thar Desert of Rajasthan
questions.rationale: Mushroom Rocks sculpted by differential eolian sandblasting are prominent in the Aravalis and Thar Desert of Rajasthan. (Key Takeaway: Eolian sandblasting creates mushroom rocks in arid desert regions.)

questions.stem: What mechanical action is exerted by growing plant roots penetrating microscopic rock joints?
questions.rationale: Expanding plant roots exert powerful radial turgor pressure that mechanically wedges rock joints apart. (Key Takeaway: Expanding root biomass acts as a mechanical wedge splitting rock joints.)

questions.stem: What chemical acid is secreted by subterranean termites and ants that corrodes rock minerals?
questions.rationale: Termites and ants secrete biochemical formic acid (HCOOH), which chemically corrodes rock-forming minerals. (Key Takeaway: Termites and ants secrete formic acid that chemically corrodes rock minerals.)

questions.stem: What is the sediment-transporting capacity of a river current moving at a velocity of 15 cm/s?
questions.rationale: A stream current moving at 15 cm/s (0.15 m/s) has the kinetic capacity to carry fine sand. (Key Takeaway: A stream current of 15 cm/s carries fine sand.)

questions.stem: Why is weathering defined as a combination of destruction and synthesis?

options.A: It destroys parent rocks and synthesizes artificial chemical fertilizers.
options.B: It destroys primary rock minerals and synthesizes new secondary minerals like clays and hydrous oxides.
options.C: It eliminates soil organisms and creates atmospheric nitrogen.
options.D: It dissolves riverbeds and forms mountain glaciers.

questions.correct_answer: B) It destroys primary rock minerals and synthesizes new secondary minerals like clays and hydrous oxides.
questions.rationale: Weathering destructively breaks down primary minerals and synthetically recombines released ions into secondary clays and sesquioxides. (Key Takeaway: Weathering unites destructive breakdown with secondary mineral synthesis.)
